newsitem.title: LEBANON: Solidere A up on Beirut Stock Exchange.
newsitem.headline: Solidere A up on Beirut Stock Exchange.

text.p: Solidere A shares edged upwards on Wednesday for the first time in seven days amid relatively busy trading on the Beirut Stock Exchange in which shares in five of the seven listed companies changed hands.
The BLOM stock index rose 0.97 percent to 910.66 and the LISPI rose 0.83 percent to 84.30.

Solidere A, which had been steady since March 18 at $10.25, close to their all-time low, rose to $10.375 while B shares were unchanged at $10.75. Turnover in Lebanon's biggest company rose to 121,745 from 105,993.

The two listed banks continued to perform strongly. Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce rose to $13.625 from $13.5 on turnover of 5,600 shares compared with 3,300 on Monday. Banque Audi was steady at $19.125 amid heavy demand. Turnover rose to 20,814 shares from 14,460.
The LIBX bank index rose 0.46 percent to 118.48.
Industrial shares Ciments Libanais and Eternit also rose in thin trading.

Some 2,500 Ciments Libanais shares changed hands at $1.2187, up from $1.1875 at which they were last traded on March 20. Eternit rose to $1.8125 from $1.75 on Monday when they were last traded. Volume was 2,000 shares.
There was no trade in the two other listed firms: Ciments Blancs and Uniceramic.
Total BSE turnover was 152,629 shares for a value of $1,741,091 against 123,693 shares for a value of $1,419,511.
